verdict.rationale: Codex documents a spec for skills: a directory with a SKILL.md that must include name and description. Its built-in creator skill interviews the user about what the skill does and when it triggers, and the built-in @plugin-creator meta-skill scaffolds the plugin.json manifest and a local marketplace entry for packaging. A community user reports building their own skills with the skill-creator skill, and a probe confirmed plugin-creator installs as a portable SKILL.md with valid frontmatter. missing for 10: a hands-on run showing an agent authoring and packaging a brand-new skill end to end with the creator/plugin-creator skills.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can author and package a new skill end to end by following the project's own spec, template, or meta-skill

citations.quote: A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md` file plus optional scripts and references. The `SKILL.md` file must include `name` and `description`.
The creator asks what the skill does, when it should trigger, and whether it should stay instruction-only or include scripts.
For the fastest setup, use the built-in `@plugin-creator` skill. It scaffolds the required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` manifest and can also generate a local marketplace entry for testing.
Use skills to design the workflow itself, then package it as a plugin when you want other people to install it.
The skills that matter most to this user are ones they build themselves with the skill-creator skill for proprietary workflows
